title: Man. Post. Cap. II §XIX: Placeus — Matt 23 / Luke 11 / Calvin on Abel cognatio
pass_a_gloss: But as to what he says, that nowhere in Scripture can the imputation of sin used in that sense be shown, that ought not to disturb us: for the phrase to impute or to be imputed sin is exceedingly rare in Scripture, and perhaps nowhere occurs except with a negation joined. But consider, most humane Reader, in what sense an equivalent phrase was used by our Lord Jesus Christ himself, Matthew 23:34. Therefore behold I send to you Prophets and wise men and scribes, and of them you will kill and crucify some, and of them you will scourge some in your Synagogues, and persecute from city to city, that upon you may come all righteous blood poured out upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar: that is, Luke explaining chapter 11:50, that from that generation may be required the blood of all the Prophets poured out from the foundation of the world. For that by those words the imputation of sin was signified cannot be denied. And so Calvin commented on those words: Although Abel was not killed by the Jews, yet Christ imputes his slaughter to them, because between them and Cain there was a certain kinship of impiety. But the inhering viciousness brings it about that between us and sinning Adam there is not just any kinship of sin, but consanguinity. Nay our inhering vice is nothing other than Adam's sin according to habit propagated into us, or like a plague or poison diffused by natural contagion. What is there therefore why it cannot be said to be imputed to us on account of that vice? See therefore, Reader, whether the Learned Man rather attacks me in this place than the Lord himself.
pass_b_english: As for the complaint that Scripture nowhere uses 'imputation of sin' in this sense: that need not unsettle us. The wording 'impute / be imputed' of sin is scarce in Scripture, and may never appear except with a negation. Kind Reader, look instead at the equivalent phrasing our Lord Jesus Christ himself used (Matthew 23:34): he sends prophets, wise men, and scribes; some will be killed and crucified, some scourged in the synagogues and hunted from city to city, so that all the righteous blood shed on earth comes upon that generation—from righteous Abel to Zechariah son of Barachiah, murdered between temple and altar. Luke puts the same point (Luke 11:50): that generation must answer for every prophet's blood shed since the world's foundation. Those words plainly signify sin's imputation. Calvin comments: Abel was not slain by the Jews, yet Christ charges them with his death because a kinship of impiety bound them to Cain. The vice that sticks in us does more still—it sets between us and sinning Adam not a loose kinship of sin but blood-relation. Our inhering vice is Adam's sin under the form of habit poured into us, like plague or poison by natural contagion. Why then may it not be said to be imputed to us for that vice's sake? Ask whether the learned man is striking at me here—or at the Lord himself.
source_text: Caeterum quod ait in Scriptura nullibi ostendi posse imputationem peccati eo sensu usurpatam, conturbare nos non debet: nam phrasis imputare vel imputari peccatum admodum rara est in Scriptura, nec forte nisi cum negatione adjuncta uspiam occurrit. Considera autem, humanissime Lector, quo sensu phrasis aequipollens ab ipso Domino nostro Jesu Christo usurpata fuerit Matth. 23.34. Propterea ecce ego mitto ad vos Prophetas & sapientes, & scribas, & ex ipsis quosdam trucidabitis & crucifigetis, & ex ipsis aliquos flagellabitis in Synagogis vestris, & persequemini ex urbe in urbem, ut veniat super vos omnis sanguis justus effusus super terram, a sanguine Abel justi usque ad sanguinem Zachariae filii Barachiae, quem occidistis inter templum & altare: hoc est, exponente Luca cap. XI. 50. ut a gente ista requiratur sanguis omnium Prophetarum effusus a jacto mundi fundamento. Quin enim illis verbis significata fuerit imputatio peccati negari nequit. Itaque sic in verba illa commentatus est Calvinus, Tametsi Abel non a Judaeis occisus est, ejus tamen necem ipsis imputat Christus, quia inter ipsos & Cain quaedam erat impietatis cognatio. Facit autem vitiositas inhaerens, ut nobis cum Adamo peccante non qualiscunque cognatio peccati, sed consanguinitas intersit. Imo vitium nostrum inhaerens nihil aliud est quam peccatum Adami secundum habitum in nos propagatum, vel instar pestis aut veneni naturali contagio diffusum. Quid est igitur, cur ob illud vitium nobis imputari dici non possit? Vide ergo, Lector, an me potius hoc loco quam ipsum Dominum, Vir Doctus impugnet.

choices.choice: Keep Abel cognatio and consanguinity application
